statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n greater than 1
k ranges over integers from 1 through n inclusive
x ranges over all real numbers
y ranges over all real numbers
floor(t) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to t
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1 and define f(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k=1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real numbers x such that for every real y, f(x) is greater than or equal to f(y), and to compute the corresponding maximum value m equal to f(x).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n greater than 1
there exists a real number x that maximizes the expression
for all real numbers y, the expression at x is greater than or equal to the expression at y

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter for the maximization problem

variables.name: y
variables.role: comparison point for defining maximality of x

witness_dependencies: the maximizing x may depend on n
the maximal value m may depend on n
